I am a PhD candidate in Economics at Georgetown University, specializing in industrial organization and energy & environmental economics. My research combines large-scale data with reduced-form and structural methods to study how market characteristics and government policy shape the U.S. renewable energy transition.

In my current projects, I examine how transmission constraints affect the environmental value of wind power across electricity markets with dissimilar fundamentals, and how different incentive designs shape wind plant maintenance and repowering decisions. My advisors are Nathan Miller, Arik Levinson, and John Rust.

Before Georgetown, I was a research analyst in the Director General's Office at the National Council of Applied Economic Research (NCAER) in New Delhi, and I trained as a chemical engineer at BITS Pilani's Hyderabad campus.
